meta.title: Nagashino
meta.war: Sengoku period: Takeda against Oda and Tokugawa
meta.subtitle: Takeda Katsuyori attacks Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu behind their palisade at Shitaragahara, and Baba Nobuharu dies covering the retreat.

sun.note: 29 June 1575 in the Julian calendar is 9 July in ours; sunrise about 04:50 local solar time. The sources give the old two-hour 'hours' (dragon ~07-09, sheep ~13-15), so times are approximate [shincho] [nsenshi].

meta.strengthNote: Traditional figures: Oda ~30,000 and Tokugawa ~8,000, Takeda 15,000 of whom 12,000 fought at Shitaragahara [shincho] [koyo] [nsenshi]; Takayanagi (1960) estimated 16-18,000 against 8-10,000 [wpja]. Shinchō kōki gives ~10,000 Takeda dead, the Tamon'in nikki 'over a thousand' of the Kai gentry [shincho] [wpja]; the 1903 history estimates the allies' killed and wounded at about 6,000, which the losses row shows [nsenshi]. Strengths inside each Takeda wing and most allied contingents are my division of the sourced totals; per-moment losses are estimates following the narrative.
meta.method: Camps, graves and the reconstructed palisade are placed from the Shinshiro battlefield markers [sites]; the allied line, the Takeda camps and the Tobigasu forts from the 1903 General Staff map georeferenced on six points (143 m) [nsmap]; the sequence from Shinchō kōki, Kōyō gunkan and the 1903 staff history [shincho] [koyo] [nsenshi]. The Takeda attack positions east of the Rengo-gawa are inferred, and positions are good to a few hundred metres.
meta.notes: The Baba contingent is featured: its note, a commander flag for Baba himself, and events in phases 3, 5, 6, 8 and 9 follow him from Maruyama to his death. Shinchō kōki makes Baba the fifth and last Takeda wave, while the Takeda tradition puts his capture of Maruyama at the start; both are shown, in that order (my reconciliation) [shincho] [koyo] [nsenshi]. The three-rank volley of 3,000 guns is a later story and is not shown [wpen] [wpja]. The palisade itself is not drawn: the allied units standing behind it mark its line, and an event at dawn marks the reconstructed section. The 2016 Shin-Tōmei expressway embankments across the field are removed from the terrain. No historical-map overlay is offered. Per-moment losses are estimates.

phases.label: Night raid
phases.title: Sakai sets out for Tobigasu
phases.text: The Takeda have crossed the Takisawa (Kansa) river and camp east of the Rengo-gawa: the right wing near Asagi, the centre at Kiyoida, the left on the heights to the south, Katsuyori's reserve west of Arumi, with 2,000 watching the castle and 1,000 in the forts on Tobigasu-yama [nsenshi] [koyo]. About 2 km to the west the allies wait behind a palisade, most of Nobunaga's 30,000 hidden in the hollow of Shitaragahara [shincho]. At 20:00 Sakai Tadatsugu leads about 4,000 men, 500 of them Nobunaga's own gunners, across the Toyokawa in the rain to circle round the Takeda [shincho] [nsenshi].
tactic: A threat to the rear
A force sent round behind the enemy turns his siege lines into a trap and leaves his army with no safe way home.
events: Sakai's column climbs by Matsuyama-goe in the dark [nsenshi] [sites]
Baba Nobuharu's 700 on the Takeda right [koyo]

phases.label: Dawn
phases.title: Tobigasu falls; facing the palisade
phases.text: At first light Sakai's column, which has climbed onto the heights south of the castle in the dark, storms the Tobigasu forts from behind with a burst of gunfire; Kawakubo Nobuzane, Saegusa Masasada and others are killed, the garrison sorties to join Sakai, and the siege huts burn [nsenshi] [wpja] [shincho]. Matsudaira Koretada of Sakai's column is killed by a Takeda counter-attack [nsenshi] [wpja]. At Shitaragahara the Takeda hear the war cries and see the smoke behind them, and Katsuyori orders an immediate attack [nsenshi]. In front of them a palisade runs along the west bank of the Rengo-gawa; Sakuma Nobumori stands outside it on the Maruyama knoll at the north end as bait, and the Ōkubo brothers outside it at the south end, placed to strike the flank [nsenshi] [sites]. Nobunaga has moved to Chausuyama in the night; Ieyasu is on Danjōyama (taken to be the Takamatsuyama of Shinchō kōki) [nsenshi] [shincho] [sites]. Baba Nobuharu holds the Takeda right opposite Maruyama [nsenshi] [koyo].
tactic: A threat to the rear
With the forts behind them lost and the siege broken, the Takeda in front of the palisade could no longer simply wait or withdraw.
events: Tobigasu stormed at first light; Kawakubo Nobuzane killed [nsenshi] [shincho]
The allied palisade along the Rengo-gawa (reconstructed today) [sites] [shincho]
Sakuma outside the palisade on Maruyama as bait [nsenshi]
phases.debate: When Tobigasu fell: the 1903 history and ja.wikipedia put the attack at first light, before the main battle, and make it the trigger for Katsuyori's attack; Shinchō kōki says Sakai's men raised their banners on Tobigasu at the hour of the dragon (about 07:00-09:00). This map follows the dawn reading [nsenshi] [wpja] [shincho].

phases.label: First wave
phases.title: Yamagata attacks in the south
phases.text: Yamagata Masakage's men come on with drums beating and are driven back by the guns [shincho]. In the 1903 history he tries to turn the allied right south of the Rengo bridge, finds the stream too deep and its banks too steep, and turns on the Ōkubo brothers outside the palisade; Kōyō gunkan counts nine clashes [nsenshi] [koyo].
tactic: Frontal assault
Attacking a prepared position head on across a stream and into massed fire.
events: Yamagata against the Ōkubo brothers: nine clashes [koyo]

phases.label: Maruyama
phases.title: Baba takes Maruyama
phases.text: On the Takeda right Baba Nobuharu attacks Sakuma Nobumori outside the palisade; Kōyō gunkan says his 700 drove about 6,000 of Sakuma's men inside it [koyo]. In the 1903 history Sakuma falls back feigning defeat, and Baba takes the Maruyama knoll and halts there instead of following him to the palisade [nsenshi]. In the centre Takeda Nobukado leads the second wave forward and is driven back by the guns [shincho].
tactic: Bait
Sakuma's men stood outside the palisade to be driven in and draw the enemy onto the guns; Baba took the ground and refused the lure.
events: Baba takes Maruyama from Sakuma (1903 history) [nsenshi] [sites]
phases.debate: Shinchō kōki, the only near-contemporary account, makes Baba the fifth and last wave. Kōyō gunkan lists his success against Sakuma first among the places where the Takeda won but gives no sequence; Maruyama and the halt come from the 1903 history, which drew on Edo compilations. This map shows both: Maruyama now and Baba's own assault later, a reconciliation of my own [shincho] [koyo] [nsenshi].

phases.label: Waves
phases.title: The third and fourth waves
phases.text: The Takeda attack in turn, each body being driven off by the guns before the next comes on [shincho]. The third wave is the Obata of West Kōzuke in red, good horsemen who attack mounted with drums beating; the fourth is Takeda Nobutoyo's men; both lose more than half their number and fall back [shincho]. The allies send out only light troops and keep firing from behind the palisade [shincho].
tactic: Field fortifications
Behind its palisade the allied army never had to come out to meet the attacks; the guns did the work.
events: The Obata of West Kōzuke attack mounted [shincho]
phases.debate: Shinchō kōki's hour of the dragon (about 07:00-09:00) is when Sakai's banners went up on Tobigasu; the 1903 history puts that at first light. The hours of the waves themselves are not recorded [shincho] [nsenshi].

phases.label: The Sanada
phases.title: The right wing breaks on the palisade
phases.text: Baba holds Maruyama and tells the Sanada brothers and Tsuchiya Masatsugu to go forward and win the honours [nsenshi]. They break into the first palisade, but the guns cut them down and Shibata Katsuie and Hashiba Hideyoshi come round the north end into their flank; Sanada Nobutsuna, his brother Masateru and Tsuchiya are killed [nsenshi] [koyo].
tactic: Combined arms
Guns behind the palisade stopped the attack; spearmen coming round the flank finished it.
events: Tsuchiya Masatsugu killed at the palisade [sites] [koyo]
The Sanada brothers break one palisade and are killed [koyo] [nsenshi]

phases.label: Fifth wave
phases.title: Baba's own attack; Yamagata falls
phases.text: Baba Mino-no-kami now leads his own men forward with drums beating, the fifth wave in Shinchō kōki, and loses many like the others [shincho]. In the south Yamagata Masakage is shot through the body and killed; one of his men carries his head back to Kai [koyo] [nsenshi]. Katsuyori commits his reserve, but the attackers melt away under the guns [nsenshi] [shincho].
tactic: Committing the reserve
Feeding the reserve into an attack that has already failed adds casualties, not weight.
events: Yamagata Masakage shot dead; his grave marker [koyo] [sites]

phases.label: Collapse
phases.title: The allies come out of the palisade
phases.text: The Takeda line comes apart. Atobe's men run first, and Anayama withdraws without having fought [nsenshi] [koyo]. Sassa Narimasa tells Nobunaga the enemy banners are wavering, and the whole allied army comes out of the palisade, the Oda in front and the Tokugawa on the Takeda left [nsenshi]. Baba sends word urging Katsuyori to withdraw [nsenshi]. Hearing of the defeat, the castle watch burns its camp and withdraws, and the garrison pursues it [nsenshi].
tactic: Pursuit
Once a beaten army turns its back, the pursuit does most of the killing.

phases.label: Rearguard
phases.title: Baba and Naitō cover the retreat
phases.text: The Takeda flee north towards Hōraiji, many drowning or falling at the river crossings [shincho] [nsenshi]. Naitō Masahide (Masatoyo in Kōyō gunkan) stands to cover Katsuyori and is killed near Miyawaki [nsenshi]. Baba, still unwounded with a few score men, refuses to leave until Katsuyori's standard is safely away [koyo] [nsenshi]. Kasai Higo gives Katsuyori his own horse and is killed [koyo]. Modern research suggests most of the senior Takeda deaths came in this retreat rather than at the palisade [wpen].
tactic: Rearguard
A few hundred men who stand and die can buy the time for their commander to escape.
events: Kasai Higo gives Katsuyori his horse and turns back to die (place approximate) [koyo]

phases.label: Suzawa
phases.title: Baba's last stand
phases.text: Once Katsuyori is out of sight, Baba turns back at Saruhashi and makes his stand on a knoll at Suzawa (出沢) above the Kansa river, calls out his name and is killed; Kōyō gunkan says he would not draw his sword [nsenshi] [koyo]. Ōta Gyūichi lists him among the Takeda dead and writes that his conduct was 'beyond compare' [shincho]. The fighting ends about 15:00; the Takeda have lost about 10,000 men by Shinchō kōki's count [shincho]. Its list of heads includes Baba, Yamagata, Tsuchiya and Sanada Nobutsuna; Naitō, Hara and Sanada Masateru are named among the dead in Kōyō gunkan and the 1903 history [shincho] [koyo] [nsenshi]. The allies lost about 6,000 killed and wounded by the 1903 history's estimate [nsenshi].
tactic: Rearguard
Baba's stand let Katsuyori cross the Kansa river and escape; the Takeda lost their senior generals in a single day.
events: Baba's grave near the castle, traditionally a head mound [sites] [wpja]
phases.debate: Where Baba died: the 1903 history and a Shinshiro marker put it at Suzawa on the Kansa river; Kōyō gunkan says 'the Nagashino bridge site', which may be the same crossing on the line of retreat. His grave near the castle is traditionally a head mound, not the place he fell. How: Kōyō gunkan has him speared by four or five men without drawing his sword; later accounts have him offer his head to Kawai Sanjūrō, a man of Ban Naomasa [nsenshi] [koyo] [sites] [wpja].

units.name: Baba Mino-no-kami Nobuharu
units.note: Baba Mino-no-kami Nobuharu (Nobufusa), aged about 61, Takeda retainer for forty years and the backbone of the right wing. With 700 men he drove Sakuma's larger force inside the palisade and took the Maruyama knoll, then (in the 1903 history) held there while the Sanada and Tsuchiya went forward [koyo] [nsenshi]. Shinchō kōki makes his own attack the fifth and last wave [shincho]. He urged Katsuyori to withdraw, covered the retreat with a few score men and, once Katsuyori was out of sight, turned to fight on a knoll at Suzawa and was killed; Ōta Gyūichi wrote that his conduct was 'beyond compare' [nsenshi] [koyo] [shincho].

units.name: Sanada Nobutsuna and Masateru
units.note: The Sanada brothers passed Baba on Maruyama, broke into the first palisade and were both killed; Nobutsuna's grave marker stands on the slope behind (strength an estimate) [koyo] [nsenshi] [sites] [shincho].

units.name: Tsuchiya Masatsugu
units.note: Tsuchiya, who had wanted to follow Shingen in death, was killed at the palisade; a marker stands at the spot (strength an estimate) [koyo] [nsenshi] [sites].

units.name: Ichijō Nobutatsu
units.note: Shingen's half-brother, on the right beside Baba; in Kōyō gunkan he rides up to Baba as the line breaks (strength an estimate) [nsenshi] [koyo].

units.name: Anayama Nobukimi
units.note: Katsuyori's kinsman withdrew without fighting, according to Kōyō gunkan (strength an estimate) [koyo] [nsenshi].

units.name: Takeda Nobukado (Shōyōken)
units.note: Shingen's brother; the second wave in Shinchō kōki, driven back by the guns (strength an estimate) [shincho] [nsenshi].

units.name: Naitō Masahide (Masatoyo)
units.note: About 1,000 men, who drove Takigawa's troops back to the palisade in the Takeda account; Naitō covered the retreat and died near Miyawaki before Baba [koyo] [nsenshi] [sites].

units.name: Hara Masatane
units.note: Killed in the attack on the palisade; his grave marker stands on the slope east of the Rengo-gawa (strength an estimate) [nsenshi] [sites] [wpja].

units.name: Annaka Kageshige and the West Kōzuke men
units.note: The rest of the centre in the 1903 order of battle, which also places Wada Narishige here (other accounts have him killed at Tobigasu); Annaka was killed (strength an estimate) [nsenshi] [wpja].

units.name: Yamagata Masakage
units.note: The first wave. His 1,500 tried to turn the allied right south of the Rengo bridge and fought the Ōkubo brothers back and forth nine times; Yamagata was shot and killed, and his grave marker stands near the stream [shincho] [koyo] [nsenshi] [sites].

units.name: Obata Nobusada (West Kōzuke 'red' men)
units.note: The third wave: the Obata of West Kōzuke in red armour, good horsemen, who attacked mounted with drums beating and were shot down; an Obata grave marker stands nearby (strength an estimate) [shincho] [nsenshi] [sites].

units.name: Takeda Nobutoyo (Tenkyū)
units.note: Katsuyori's cousin; the fourth wave, which also failed at the palisade (strength an estimate) [shincho] [nsenshi].

units.name: Oyamada, Atobe, Amari and Ogasawara
units.note: The rest of the left wing; Atobe's men were the first to run and Amari was killed (strength an estimate) [nsenshi] [koyo] [sites].

units.name: Takeda Katsuyori (main body)
units.note: The general reserve under Katsuyori, west of Arumi on the 20th; Katsuyori watched from Saino-kami, committed his men late and escaped north with a few hundred (strength an estimate) [nsenshi] [sites] [wpja].

units.name: Mochizuki Nobunaga and Takeda Nobutomo
units.note: The rest of the reserve, sent forward late; Mochizuki Nobunaga, Katsuyori's cousin, was killed (the 1903 history names Mochizuki Nobumasa; strength an estimate) [nsenshi] [wpja].

units.name: Castle watch (Oyamada Masayuki, Kōsaka Masazumi, Muroga)
units.note: Two thousand left west of the castle to keep the garrison in. In the 1903 history they held on after Tobigasu fell, then burned their camp and withdrew once news came of the defeat at Shitaragahara; the garrison pursued and killed Kōsaka Masazumi and about 200 men. ja.wikipedia instead has Sakai's column sweeping them from Arumi in the morning (strength from Kōyō gunkan and the 1903 history) [nsenshi] [koyo] [wpja].

units.name: Tobigasu forts (Kawakubo Nobuzane)
units.note: Five forts on the heights south of the castle, stormed from behind at first light. Kawakubo Nobuzane, Saegusa Masasada, Gomi, Wada Narishige and Nawa Murisuke were killed there; the 1903 history counts about 370 Takeda heads [nsenshi] [wpja] [shincho] [nsmap].

units.name: Sakuma Nobumori
units.note: Placed outside the palisade around Maruyama as bait in the 1903 history; Kōyō gunkan has Baba's 700 drive about 6,000 of his men inside it [nsenshi] [koyo] [wpja].

units.name: Ikeda, Mizuno, Gamō, Mori and others
units.note: Contingents named east of the four hills in the 1903 order of battle, shown together at the north end of the line (strength an estimate) [nsenshi].

units.name: Niwa Nagahide
units.note: Moved forward onto Arumihara facing east with Takigawa and Hashiba (strength an estimate) [shincho] [nsenshi].

units.name: Takigawa Kazumasu
units.note: Behind the palisade on Arumihara, facing east; about 3,000 in Kōyō gunkan, driven back to the palisade by Naitō [shincho] [koyo].

units.name: Arquebusiers of the five commanders (Sassa, Maeda, Nonomura, Fukutomi, Ban)
units.note: About 1,000 guns drawn from many units and put under five commanders along the palisade [shincho]. This was not the army's whole firepower: the contingents' own guns, the Tokugawa guns and those levied from other lords are uncounted, so the total was probably well over 1,500 [wpja] [wpen]. The later '3,000 firing by turns' is a myth [wpen] [wpja]. Ban Naomasa's man Kawai Sanjūrō is credited with taking Baba's head [wpja].

units.name: Hashiba Hideyoshi
units.note: On Arumihara with Takigawa and Niwa; in the 1903 history he and Shibata came round the north end to take the Sanada in flank (camp marker; strength an estimate) [shincho] [nsenshi] [sites].

units.name: Shibata Katsuie
units.note: With Nobunaga at Gokurakujiyama in the 1903 order of battle, then round the north flank with Hashiba; his presence and the flank attack rest on the 1903 history alone (Shinchō kōki's chapter does not name him; strength an estimate) [nsenshi].

units.name: Oda Nobunaga's horse guards
units.note: Nobunaga camped at Gokurakujiyama and kept his 30,000 hidden in the hollow [shincho]; the 1903 history has him move to Chausuyama on the night of the 20th (strength an estimate) [nsenshi] [sites].

units.name: Oda Nobutada
units.note: Nobunaga's heir, camped on Shinmidōyama (Tenjinyama in the 1903 history) in reserve (exact hill uncertain; strength an estimate) [shincho] [nsenshi].

units.name: Kitabatake Nobukatsu and Inaba Ittetsu
units.note: In reserve on Midōyama in the 1903 order of battle (strength an estimate) [nsenshi].

units.name: Oda guns with Sakai (Kanamori Nagachika)
units.note: 500 of Nobunaga's own guns and his inspectors, Kanamori Nagachika among them, sent with Sakai's column; Shinchō kōki gives the whole column about 4,000 (the division between this unit and Sakai's is an estimate) [shincho] [nsenshi].

units.name: Tokugawa Ieyasu
units.note: Ieyasu camped on Takamatsuyama on the Tatsumi slope, identified locally with Danjōyama, where Nobunaga joined him to watch the battle (camp marker; strength an estimate) [shincho] [nsenshi] [sites].

units.name: Honda Tadakatsu
units.note: Behind the Tokugawa palisade (strength an estimate) [nsenshi].

units.name: Sakakibara Yasumasa
units.note: Behind the Tokugawa palisade (strength an estimate) [nsenshi].

units.name: Ishikawa Kazumasa, Torii Mototada, Hiraiwa and others
units.note: The rest of the Tokugawa line in the 1903 order of battle (strength an estimate) [nsenshi].

units.name: Ōkubo Tadayo and Tadasuke
units.note: Outside the palisade on the allied right, placed to strike the flank; the brothers fought Yamagata's men back and forth nine times (camp marker; strength an estimate) [nsenshi] [koyo] [sites].

units.name: Matsudaira Nobuyasu
units.note: Ieyasu's heir, on Matsuoyama behind the Tokugawa line in the 1903 order of battle (hill and strength uncertain) [nsenshi].

units.name: Sakai Tadatsugu's column
units.note: About 2,000 picked Tokugawa archers and gunners with their commanders (Shinchō kōki: about 4,000 with the Oda guns; the 1903 history: about 3,000). They crossed the Toyokawa at night in rain, climbed by Matsuyama-goe, stormed the Tobigasu forts from behind at dawn and joined the garrison, cutting the Takeda line of retreat; Matsudaira Koretada was killed by a Takeda counter-attack [shincho] [nsenshi] [wpja] [sites].

units.name: Nagashino garrison (Okudaira Sadamasa)
units.note: About 500 men who had held the castle for weeks; they sortied to join Sakai once Tobigasu fell, and pursued the castle watch when it withdrew [wpen] [shincho] [nsenshi].

hq.name: Baba Nobuharu
hq.note: Baba led from the front; the flag follows him from Maruyama to Suzawa [koyo] [nsenshi].

hq.name: Oda Nobunaga
hq.note: On the morning of the 21st Nobunaga went up to Ieyasu's camp on Takamatsuyama to watch and direct [shincho].
